#recipeideas #gelatin  Gelatin is collagen just in a different form. Collagen is a structural protein found in animal tissues like skin, bones, and connective tissue. When you take that collagen and cook it (heat + water), it breaks down into gelatin. What actually happens: 	•	Collagen has a tight, triple-helix structure (very strong and rigid) 	•	When heated, that structure unwinds and partially breaks down 	•	This creates a softer, more digestible form → gelatin So when you see: “Unflavored natural gelatin (bovine)” 	•	“Bovine” = comes from cows 	•	“Unflavored” = no additives 	•	“Gelatin” = collagen that has been hydrolyzed by heat

Where does collagen go after you drink it? Collagen supplements don't travel intact from your stomach straight to your skin or joints. Your digestive system breaks collagen down into smaller components, including amino acids and peptides, which are then absorbed and used by the body. Collagen is particularly rich in amino acids such as glycine and proline, which are among the building blocks involved in protein and collagen production. Vitamin C also plays an important role in normal collagen formation. Research has also explored whether certain collagen peptides may have signaling effects, so the story isn't simply “collagen gets destroyed.” The bigger takeaway? You're supplying raw materials, not shipping finished collagen directly to your skin. 💬 What benefit are you hoping to get from collagen? #collagen #collagenpeptides #collagenpowder #vitaminc #glycine #proline #protein #aminoacids #skinhealth #jointhealth #supplements #nutritiontok
